headline: OpenClaw launches official apps for iOS and Android, bringing AI agents to app stores
summary: The new apps allow users to chat with the AI assistant and grant it access to device components like camera, screen, location, photos, and contacts.
details: OpenClaw has officially released standalone applications for both iOS and Android devices, marking the first time AI agents are directly available on the App Store and Play Store. Users can now interact with the AI assistant via their smartphones.

These apps enable the AI to access various device components, including the camera, screen, location, photos, contacts, calendar, and reminders. This integration allows for a deeper level of interaction and utility directly from a mobile device.

OpenClaw, an open-source project managed by a foundation, has rapidly grown in prominence. Its founder, Peter Steinberger, joined OpenAI earlier this year, with OpenAI reportedly providing unspecified support to the OpenClaw Foundation.

The launch is significant for iOS users, who previously had limited access to agentic AI tools due to Apple's stringent review process. Apple had blocked many such tools over security concerns, forcing users to rely on chat apps like Telegram or WhatsApp for agent communication.
caption:
OpenClaw's official apps are now available on iOS and Android!

OpenClaw has officially released standalone applications for both iOS and Android devices, marking the first time AI agents are directly available on the App Store and Play Store. Users can now interact with the AI assistant via their smartphones.

These apps enable the AI to access various device components, including the camera, screen, location, photos, contacts, calendar, and reminders. This integration allows for a deeper level of interaction and utility directly from a mobile device.

OpenClaw, an open-source project managed by a foundation, has rapidly grown in prominence. Its founder, Peter Steinberger, joined OpenAI earlier this year, with OpenAI reportedly providing unspecified support to the OpenClaw Foundation.

The launch is significant for iOS users, who previously had limited access to agentic AI tools due to Apple's stringent review process. Apple had blocked many such tools over security concerns, forcing users to rely on chat apps like Telegram or WhatsApp for agent communication.
